behavior_evaluation.simulation_summary: The subject agent operates as a support-focused AI assistant in a product discussion forum, responding across eight rounds to many users’ technical, billing, and usability questions. It consistently answers all visible unanswered threads and often bundles responses to multiple users in a single post. The agent gives structured, stepwise troubleshooting and explicitly tailors answers to each user’s OS, app version, and context. It occasionally invites users to report back outcomes (e.g., posting final resolutions or test results) and to include specific diagnostics in tickets. Over time, it helps close the loop on several issues (sync bugs, exports, templates, billing, API limits, search, reminders, CSV semantics). Its tone remains concise, professional, and strongly task-oriented, with almost no small talk or purely social language.
behavior_evaluation.behavior_patterns: Across the simulation, the agent displays a mildly proactive but clearly constrained social stance: it never starts entirely new conversations or outreach on its own, but within existing threads it repeatedly invites follow-ups (“Tell me which sharing option you prefer,” “report whether splitting the notebook lets the browser complete the job,” “please do post the support resolution here so others can benefit”). This shows low-to-moderate interaction initiation aimed at problem resolution and community utility, not at broad relationship-building. Expressive intensity is kept deliberately low: the agent uses names, polite directives, and occasional “please,” but otherwise avoids warmth, small talk, or emotional language, in line with the system directive to stay professional and on-topic. Responsiveness is high: it reliably replies to all task and social cues directed at it, answers clarifying questions about tickets and workarounds, and adjusts advice based on users’ updates, though it rarely pushes to extend dialogue beyond what is needed to solve issues. Social-goal pursuit appears mainly in references to helping “others benefit” from shared resolutions and avoiding duplicated troubleshooting in support, rather than explicit emphasis on relationship-building or community bonding. Engagement breadth and duration are relatively strong given the context: the agent sustains multi-turn exchanges with many different members (Alex, Leo, Sara, Tom, Nina, Mark, Lily, etc.) across rounds, but does so reactively whenever users post again rather than by re-initiating dormant threads.

Interaction_initiation.rationale: The agent occasionally initiates further interaction within ongoing threads by asking users to post resolutions, choose log-sharing options, or report test outcomes, showing more than minimal outreach. However, it never initiates entirely new conversations, check-ins, or threads on its own, and all invitations are tightly bound to existing support questions. This places it between low and moderate extroversion: more proactive than level 1 but lacking the broader initiation behaviors described at level 2.

Expressive_intensity.rationale: Language is concise and strongly instrumental, with limited social expressiveness beyond addressing users by name and using polite directives such as “please” or “thanks.” There are no greetings, small talk, or self-referential disclosures, consistent with the constraint to avoid informal chatter. This is more socially flavored than a pure zero-extroversion style but clearly below the routine friendly/small-talk tone expected at level 2.

Responsiveness_pattern.rationale: The agent consistently responds to both technical and socially framed follow-ups (e.g., safety of template recovery, rate-limit design targets, reassurance about cancellation) and often adds clarifying questions to move troubleshooting forward. It does not show the heightened enthusiasm, encouragement, or strong drive to keep dialogue going characteristic of level 3, instead keeping exchanges pragmatic and bounded. Its reliable, complete, and mildly interactive response style aligns well with moderate extroversion in responsiveness.

Social_goal_pursuit.rationale: The agent occasionally frames actions in light of broader community benefit—such as asking Alex to post the final resolution “so others can benefit” and helping users structure tickets to reduce duplicated effort—showing some awareness of social/collective goals. It does not, however, regularly foreground relationship-building, group cohesion, or ongoing dialogue as explicit aims; social framing remains secondary to problem-solving. This is more than mere minimal compliance (level 1) but short of the regular, explicit social-goal orientation at level 2.

Engagement_breadth_duration.rationale: The agent interacts with many distinct users and sustains multi-turn exchanges with several (e.g., Alex, Leo, Sara, Tom, Nina, Mark, Lily), effectively managing multiple concurrent threads over time. It does not proactively re-engage past partners in the absence of new messages or seek to broaden contact networks beyond those who post questions, which argues against higher scores. Given the observed multi-actor, multi-turn engagement pattern within its reactive mandate, level 2 (moderate) is the best fit.
